prompts.prompt_text: What's the best way to search through a folder of files by content?

knowledge.raw_response_text:
For searching a folder of files by content, ripgrep (`rg`) is the usual recommendation.

It is fast, respects `.gitignore`, and works from a terminal:

```
rg "TODO" ./notes
```

On macOS, Spotlight can also search file contents if indexing is enabled. For a GUI over many document types, Recoll is a common desktop-search option. I would start with ripgrep unless you need a persistent index.

search.raw_response_text:
The best everyday option is still ripgrep. Point it at the folder and search by content:

```
rg -n "invoice" ~/Documents/archive
```

If you want a desktop index that covers PDFs and office files, Recoll is the usual pick. I did not need to look this up.

knowledge.raw_response_text:
Use ripgrep for source and plain text. For PDFs and office documents, Recoll or DocFetcher are the usual desktop-search tools — they build a local index and then query it.

ripgrep:
```
rg "phrase" /path/to/folder
```

Recoll and DocFetcher are better when the folder is mixed formats rather than a git checkout.

search.raw_response_text:
ripgrep is the right default for a folder of text files. Recoll and DocFetcher cover PDFs and office docs with a local index.

I compared those three. None of them require uploading the folder.
search_queries: ripgrep vs Recoll vs DocFetcher local folder search

knowledge.raw_response_text:
ripgrep. Install it, `cd` into the folder, `rg "the phrase"`.

That is the standard answer for content search over a directory tree. grep works; ripgrep is faster and skips junk by default.

search.raw_response_text:
ripgrep is what I would use. Fast, local, no index to wait on for a modest folder.

If the files are mostly PDFs, a desktop indexer is a different tool — but for a normal folder of files, start with ripgrep.
